title: 3D entity-family consumer and peer test-boundary audit
mode: Primary-source standards, project documentation, live peer issue/PR, and local source review; research-only plan refinement
worktreeState: Dirty shared worktree; inspected only plan and relevant writer source, preserved unrelated changes
scope: Reconcile FreeCAD's documented DXF importer/exporter routes by entity family, including explicit MESH and 3DFACE applicability.
Cross-check the current local MESH and ACIS-carrier DXF writer boundaries against Autodesk's DXF contract.
Refresh ezdxf, LibreDWG, and ACadSharp capability/test-evidence boundaries for explicit 3D and ACIS paths.
Refine existing implementation and composed native/peer gates without adding dependencies or promoting support claims.

sources.name: Autodesk DXF references
sources.observed: The 3DSOLID DXF shell uses AcDbModelerGeometry, group 70, proprietary data groups 1/3, and an AcDb3dSolid subclass with optional history group 350. This shell contract does not establish payload syntax or geometric semantics.

sources.name: FreeCAD official Draft DXF guide
sources.observed: The built-in C++ and legacy Python DXF importer lists differ. The legacy list includes 3DFACE while neither published list names MESH; the guide says stock FreeCAD cannot read embedded ACIS solids. The C++ exporter emits selected straight edge linework from 3D faces, limits curved-edge output to XY-parallel cases, and may duplicate lines; the legacy exporter flattens 3D objects to 2D views. Neither is a general solid round-trip oracle. DWG import remains converter-to-DXF followed by the selected importer.

sources.name: ezdxf 1.4.5 ACIS and drawing documentation
sources.observed: The ACIS API documents bounded SAT/SAB load/export, SAT 700 for DXF R2000-R2010 and SAB 21800 for R2013/R2018, and limited supported ACIS entities. Unsupported entities can become NONE_ENTITY and lose data when exported. Body-to-mesh extraction loses faces with curved boundaries; the drawing add-on does not render ACIS and projects 3D into XY.

sources.name: LibreDWG 0.13.4 manual
sources.observed: The manual describes distinct 3DSOLID SAT/SAB carrier, wireframe, silhouette, revision, and history fields. Its coverage chapter separately lists MESH, BODY, and POLYLINE/VERTEX families among missing example-corpus test cases, demonstrating that data structures/project coverage declarations and sample-backed test coverage are different measures.

sources.name: ACadSharp live writer issue and pull request
sources.observed: Issue #1195 reports silent 3DSOLID/REGION omission in ACadSharp 3.4.9 DXF output. PR #1150 remains open/undeployed; its comments describe selected TrueView opens, later schema redesign, and a post-refactor repeated-group-310 reader concern. These are branch-specific reports, not released behavior or independent semantic qualification.

sources.name: Local current-worktree writer source
sources.observed: The current checkout emits version-dependent typed MESH DXF with AcDbSubDMesh; modeler-geometry DXF emission contains qualified SAT-v1/AC1027 SAB gates and refuses unqualified carriers. This is source inspection only; no test or native application was run.

assessment.planImpact: Corrects FreeCAD acceptance to an importer/entity-specific matrix: built-in documented subset, legacy 3DFACE, MESH not documented, and stock ACIS not applicable. Tightens distinction among DXF carrier handling, limited ezdxf mesh projection, LibreDWG per-family test coverage, and ACadSharp branch-only writing. Existing implementation gates and infrequent composed native/peer checks remain in place.

method.kind: Read-only review of official documentation, current primary project sources, live issue/PR state, and local current-worktree writer code
method.limitations: Project documentation and live issue/PR pages can change; no peer artifact was pinned, built, or run. FreeCAD documentation establishes a published importer scope, not actual runtime behavior for MESH. Local source inspection does not establish independent reader or native-application acceptance. No claim was made about a local defect or general format support.
